feedback: The candidate maintains the geometry and sensor layout from the previous iteration, which was well balanced and stable. The controller parameters have been adjusted to reduce base_speed from 1.2 to 1.0, and PID gains kp and kd have been lowered to 6 and 2 respectively, while ki is increased to 1.0. This aligns with the earlier evidence from iteration 0 where the robot performed well on oval and s-bend tracks but failed the slalom due to overshoot and oscillations. The reduced base_speed and softer PID gains should help improve stability and reduce steering oscillation, potentially improving slalom completion. The integral gain increase aims to better correct steady-state errors. The sensor weights and line loss strategy remain unchanged, as they provided good line detection and recovery. Depending on the next race results, if the robot still fails to complete the slalom or shows high steering oscillation, consider further reducing base_speed or tuning PID gains. If the robot completes with high rms_error, try increasing ki further or adjusting sensor weights to improve line tracking precision. Overall, this candidate is a reasonable revision to test the impact of reduced speed and softer control on challenging tracks.
requested_changes: controller.base_speed: 0.9 if slalom completion still fails (iteration 0 evidence)
controller.kp: 5 and controller.kd: 1.5 if steering oscillation remains high (iteration 0 evidence)
controller.ki: 1.5 if rms_error remains high on curves (iteration 0 evidence)
